summary.oneLiner: Sarda Energy has successfully pivoted from a cyclical steel player to an integrated energy-mining major, with FY26 EBITDA tripling to INR 2,025 cr driven by a 84% surge in thermal generation and record coal output. The strategic roadmap focuses on doubling thermal capacity to 1,200 MW by FY30 and quadrupling mining capacity, while re-entering steel capex (pellet expansion) to capture upcoming iron ore supply in Chhattisgarh.

one-line thesis: Sarda Energy has successfully pivoted from a cyclical steel player to an integrated energy-mining major, with FY26 EBITDA tripling to INR 2,025 cr driven by a 84% surge in thermal generation and record coal output. The strategic roadmap focuses on doubling thermal capacity to 1,200 MW by FY30 and quadrupling mining capacity, while re-entering steel capex (pellet expansion) to capture upcoming iron ore supply in Chhattisgarh.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,258 cr (Q4), INR 5,928 cr (FY26, +23% YoY); EBITDA: INR 352 cr (Q4), INR 2,025 cr (FY26, +44% YoY, ~34% margin); PAT: INR 155 cr (Q4, +53% YoY), INR 1,109 cr (FY26, +58% YoY); Order Book: N/A (Power sold via merchant/PPA); Net Debt: INR 215 cr (down 85% YoY from INR 1,566 cr), Net Debt/EBITDA <1x. One-offs: Q4 impacted by planned shutdown of 30MW captive unit and 300MW turbine maintenance; Hydropower seasonal slowdown.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Driven by efficiency gains, full-year Rehar hydro, and solar commissioning in FY27; Margins: Stability expected via shift to 300MW medium/long-term PPAs (up from 100MW); Order Inflow: Secured 300MW PPA capacity for next year; Capex: INR 500-700 cr annually for FY27-28 (excl. SKS expansion); SKS expansion capex TBD pending DPR, commissioning targeted FY30-31.
order book & pipeline: Power sales mix shifting: FY26 mostly merchant (short-term); FY27 guidance sees 200-300MW under medium/long-term PPAs providing visibility vs volatile spot prices (spot ~INR 3.75/unit in Q4).
segment / subsidiary detail: Energy (2/3 of EBITDA): Thermal gen 4,155 MU (+84% YoY); Hydro 661 MU (+31% YoY). Mining: Gare Palma IV/7 hit max limit 1.8 MTPA; Shahpur West commissioning FY27. Metals: Pellets 0.83 MT (record); Sponge Iron 0.35 MT (record); HB Wire 40k MT (record).
growth verticals / optionality: 1) SKS Power brownfield expansion to 1,200 MW by FY30 (land/fuel ready, EC pending); 2) Coal mine capacity quadrupling (Shahpur West, Gare Palma IV/5, Bartunga, Senduri); 3) Hydropower pipeline: 66 MW (Arunachal) + 74 MW (Chhattisgarh) + 25 MW (Rehar operational); 4) Pellet plant expansion (0.9 to 2.0 MTPA) to capture new Chhattisgarh iron ore mines.
margins & cost dynamics: Thermal realization >INR 5/unit; Q4 exchange price ~INR 3.75/unit. Coal index up 8-9% YoY due to import disruptions/West Asia crisis. Iron ore prices softening (NMDC/OMC cuts) offsetting coal cost pressure for steel segment. PPA mix shift expected to stabilize realizations vs merchant volatility.
capex / expansion: FY27-28 annual capex INR 500-700 cr (Hydro, Mines, Solar, TG replacement). Pellet expansion: INR 500 cr over 2.5 years. SKS 600MW expansion: Major capex starts FY28 post-EC, completion FY30-31. Hydro projects (Khuitam, 3x CH projects): 3-4 year execution timeline.
capital allocation: Net cash positive standalone; Consolidated liquidity INR 2,380 cr. Record 200% dividend recommended. Strategic M&A: Acquired majority stake in Adishankar Khuitam (66 MW Hydro). Treasury: Minor Godawari Power share purchase (<1% of liquidity) deemed normal treasury ops, no major stake buildup planned.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical: West Asia/Middle East conflict impacting oil prices, inflation, and global steel demand. Regulatory: Delays in environment clearances for SKS expansion and new mines. Market: Chinese steel export dumping (though safeguard measures in place); Volatility in merchant power prices. Operational: Seasonal hydro variability; Execution delays in brownfield expansions.
management quality / tone: Confident and transformational; Emphasizes shift from cyclical commodity player to stable energy-mining integrated model. Prudent on steel cycle (believes bottomed out but wary of global war impact). Aggressive on capacity doubling with strong balance sheet support.
non-obvious takeaways: Management is exploring demerger/separation of the Renewable Energy business specifically, not the entire power vertical. Pellet capex revival is strategically timed to coincide with state-owned (CMDC) iron ore mine auctions in Chhattisgarh over next 2-2.5 years, securing raw material for expanded capacity.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
